protocol.question: Can the same network learn exact action values on known and fresh layouts?
protocol.hypothesis: Removing exploration and bootstrapped targets may expose a different fitting or transfer limit.

dataset.layout_key_description: walls + pellet + rules, ignoring spawn and clock

optimizer.name: Adam
optimizer.sampling: 64 uniform states without replacement within each batch

gates.scope: each seed, final checkpoint, greedy only; fresh above pooled random

metric_definitions.q95_abs_q_error: 95th percentile of per-state mean absolute error across four actions
metric_definitions.optimal_action_rate: optimal greedy actions among winnable states; tie tolerance1e-6
metric_definitions.mean_signed_q_bias: prediction minus exact value, averaged over all four actions and states
metric_definitions.mean_action_regret: unconditional mean exact regret of learned greedy argmax
metric_definitions.loss_aggregate: mean pre-update minibatch SmoothL1 over preceding updates_in_window (normally100)

limitations: Privileged exact labels remove both exploration and bootstrapped targets; this does not isolate a single RL failure cause.
All possible position/clock states on the selected layouts are supervised; this is not an RL sample-efficiency comparison.
Historical RL receives the same fresh panel; physical overlap with its training layouts is reported without replacing the panel.
Three initializations share one selected training bank; seed ranges are not confidence intervals.
